$comment: Swift noise table (handoff §2: construct tables are data, not code). What a call on a typed value must NOT be drawn as. The primary rule is shape, not names: a receiver whose type is wrapped in a collection is a call on the Standard Library's Array/Dictionary/Set, a framework type, and is dropped by the same path that drops Text(...) and JSONEncoder(). The name lists below are the second guard, applied only when the member is declared nowhere in the pack AND the receiver is a concrete struct/class/enum, never a protocol (a protocol requirement may legitimately be named like a stdlib operation).

collection_wrappers.$comment: Type wrapper → the Standard Library type the call is really on. Optional is transparent: `x?.f()` calls f on the wrapped type.

synthesized_static_members.$comment: Compiler-synthesized static members a user type has without declaring them, with the type they evaluate to. `Self` is the enclosing type and is handled by shape. An undeclared static member NOT listed here has an unknown type and its call is not drawn (never assumed to be a singleton instance).

view_modifiers.$comment: SwiftUI View-protocol extension methods. Dropped only when the receiver type is declared in the pack, conforms to View/ViewModifier/Scene/Widget, and declares no member of this name anywhere in the pack.

stdlib_sequence_members.$comment: Sequence, Collection, RangeReplaceableCollection and Dictionary operations. The fallback guard for a receiver whose collection wrapper could not be recovered.
